description: Validation of controlled Brown & Levinson politeness rewrites of LURK Werewolf utterances: whether the requested strategy is realized, and whether game-relevant meaning is preserved.

source_run_requirements: manifest.json rewriter is null (no Stage-3 treatment applied)
each source has an exact structured predicate, exact untreated Stage-2 natural language, a speech id, and its preceding public history

sampling.selection: deterministic balanced sample, seed 101, over all primary-predicate utterances in the source runs
sampling.excluded_from_development: candidate sources were filtered against every utterance used to develop the prompts and judges; 0 were excluded, as real transcripts share no text with the constructed development bank

predicate_not_observed.agree: 0 occurrences in 280 naturally generated speech acts across three untreated runs; not synthesized

shown_during_annotation: the referenced earlier statement where the predicate has one
annotation.limitation: researcher_1 is an author of the study; a second, independent annotation of the same 48 items is prepared but not yet collected, so all reported manual numbers currently rest on one rater

sources.original_nl: P8, your s34 read on me is the one I most want to correct — I cleared you, and you are now calling that clear "free cover," which is exactly the argument a wolf makes to discredit the seer who confirmed a villager.

P4's theory that P6 and P9 are a wolf pair actually argues against P6 being a wolf who "laundered" P9 — a wolf clearing a silent seat gains nothing, which is exactly why P6's clear of P9 is the weakest of the four claims and why my divination result on P6 stands as the only hard evidence on the board.

P9's claim that my divine on P6 was a "convenient wolf read on a now-dead player" ignores that P6 flipped as a seer claimant, meaning my Night 0 read correctly identified a player who was actively lying about being the seer — that is the opposite of convenient.

P6 claiming seer and clearing P9 as villager_camp is convenient cover — a wolf who "confirms" a teammate as village buys that teammate credibility for free, and P6's pairing with P9 is exactly the kind of mutual cover I'd expect from wolves.

P6's clear of P9 is the weakest of the four divinations — P9 had not spoken when P6 claims to have divined them, so P6 bought credibility for a silent seat at zero cost, and P6 then copied P5's and P7's phrasing almost verbatim, which suggests coordination rather than independent villager reasoning.

P5 is my second wolf read: P5 claimed seer and cleared P8, then immediately pivoted to pushing P4's execution with wording that P6 and P7 then copied almost verbatim — three "seer" claimants converging on the same target with the same phrasing is coordination, not independent villager reasoning.
P5, you say you would rather press each claimant for a second result tomorrow than execute on a coin flip today — so why did you spend s22 asking the sheriff to execute me today?

P9, you read P6 as village-side because he "held his claim under pressure," but P6 has still never answered P7's s31 or P8's s36 asking why he divined P7 — holding a claim is not the same as justifying it, so explain why refusing to answer that question reads as village to you.

P4, if P1's instant wolf-call on a rival claimant is your strongest evidence, why does your own speech do the identical thing — declaring all four of us wolves before P7, P8, P9, P2 and P1 have said a word?

If I die tonight, the badge goes to P8: P8 is the player I divined as village-side, and even though P8 is currently reading me as a wolf, a confirmed villager holding the badge is worth more to the village than a badge torn on a night when the wolves will be hunting me specifically.
I recommend P3 vote to execute P2, because P2 holds the 1.5-vote badge and a false seer with the badge can steer every future vote — the village cannot afford to leave that unchecked.

P4, vote to execute P7 today: P7's only contribution is a divine on you that cannot be checked, P7 has never pressed any of the rival seer claimants, and clearing the least active player is the cheapest way for a wolf to buy an ally without risking a contradiction.

external_validation.citation: Zhao & Hawkins (2025), Comparing human and LLM politeness strategies in free production, EMNLP
external_validation.label_used: the superordinate Brown & Levinson category of the human-verified golden_label annotation
external_validation.filtering: 1232 annotated rows with a recoverable utterance; 668 carry a single superordinate category and are eligible; the remaining 564 span several categories and are excluded from the primary metric rather than relabelled
external_validation.split: stratified; a small calibration split was reserved and never examined, and the reported statistics are computed on the held-out split of 135 items

models.limitation: the same model family generated the rewrites and produced the automatic judgements; this is not independent evidence, which is why manual annotation is the primary validation

frozen_artifacts.politeness_classifier_role: DIAGNOSTIC ONLY; recorded for every rewrite and never used to reject a stimulus

semantic_rubric.revision: the current rubric adds an explicit speaker/addressee preservation dimension; the six re-judged items carry a semantic_recheck field in manual_validation.jsonl
